To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a database application can be modeled as a set of transactions, each transaction is modeled as a set (sequence) of database operations, and each operation is modeled as an I/O request to the disk.

the database application class is highly sensitive to network delays and that the traffic characteristics of database applications depend on the database size, database structure and the type of transaction.
the traffic of distributed applications is bursty, and its characteristics are a function of the number of clients, the number of transactions, and the transaction size.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (1) the characterization of distributed database application traffic; (2) the development of a methodology to accurately compute the traffic descriptors for distributed database applications; and (3) the development of an analytical model for distributed database applications that can be used for network design, performance evaluation, and resource allocation.
characterizing the network traffic of distributed database applications in a network environment.
developing a methodology to characterize the traffic of distributed databases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the traffic generated by distributed database systems is bursty, has a large number of short flows and is highly variable, but the traffic is predictable and can be accurately characterized using the proposed methodology.
the traffic characteristics of a distributed database system depend upon the application's workload, the network topology and the database system architecture.
the network traffic characteristics of a distributed database application are primarily a function of the application's workload, the network topology and the network protocol used.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the traffic generated from a distributed database system can be classified into two broad categories, namely, database access traffic and database transaction management traffic.
a database transaction processing application can be modeled as a Poisson process with a bursty arrival pattern and the transaction duration can be modeled by an Erlang distribution.
we have shown how the application level characteristics of a distributed database application map into the network traffic characteristics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the traffic characteristics of distributed database applications can be accurately modeled by the superposition of two traffic sources: a bursty traffic source, and a background traffic source.
the traffic of distributed databases is bursty and the burstiness is due to the nature of the database transactions.
the traffic characteristics of a distributed database application are a function of the application scenario and the database workload.
